claims.text: High-entropy alloys have superior dynamic mechanical behavior compared with conventional alloys.
Severe lattice distortion is responsible for the superior dynamic mechanical behavior of high-entropy alloys.
A multi-principal-element configuration produces significant lattice distortion in a single-phase high-entropy alloy.
Lattice distortions impede dislocation mobility under high-strain-rate loading.
Reduced dislocation mobility produces a strengthened response under dynamic loading.
Reduced dislocation mobility permits improved ductility under dynamic loading.
Lattice-distortion-mediated hindrance of dislocation motion increases strain-rate sensitivity.
Lattice-distortion-mediated hindrance of dislocation motion increases work-hardening capability.
Under high-strain-rate testing, the high-entropy alloy will have a higher yield stress than the conventional-alloy baseline.
Under high-strain-rate testing, the high-entropy alloy will have a greater work-hardening rate than the conventional-alloy baseline.
Under high-strain-rate testing, the high-entropy alloy will have greater strain-rate sensitivity than the conventional-alloy baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies to single-phase high-entropy alloys at ambient temperature under dynamic loading.
The proposed mechanism may cease to apply when high-temperature diffusion dominates deformation.
The proposed mechanism may cease to apply when phase transformations dominate deformation.
Dynamic strain aging may compete with the proposed lattice-distortion mechanism and influence dynamic mechanical performance.
